risks.note: Explicitly listed under MD&A THREATS: 'Heightened competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market, which may exert pressure on yields and margins despite sustained demand.' This bears directly on the two KPIs management runs the business on - average blended yield (2.12% per month) and fleet utilisation - and the MD&A concedes the Company relied on 'value-led customer engagement, disciplined asset deployment and calibrated commercial interventions to sustain yields and margins'.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity in the domestic crane rental market

risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Reliance on specialised equipment imported from Germany and China exposes the Company to procurement delays, logistics risks, and potential changes in customs duties.' For an asset-heavy rental model where growth is delivered by adding high-capacity cranes, procurement lead-time or duty changes directly gate the capex programme; the MoU with Action Construction Equipment Limited for indigenously manufactured heavy cranes is the stated structural response.

MD&A THREATS: 'Delays in project execution due to seasonal factors or customer site readiness may result in 10-15% of the order book carrying over into the next financial period.' This is a quantified, recurring revenue-recognition risk on a business whose visibility case rests on the order book, and it sits alongside the Rs 165 crore of FY2025-26 capex that was itself deferred to 2026-27.
risks.risk: Execution and external delays causing order-book slippage

risks.note: MD&A THREATS and segment commentary: revenue can fluctuate in the EPC businesses because of the percentage-of-completion method, 'especially in the early stages of a project'. As the Wind EPC and Project EPC verticals are the stated diversification engines and are scaling from a low base, reported performance may vary between periods independent of underlying demand; the Company states it selects contracts on execution capability and profitability thresholds.
risks.risk: Revenue volatility in the EPC businesses under percentage-of-completion

risks.note: MD&A THREATS: 'Higher operating costs in international markets such as Saudi Arabia, driven by manpower requirements, regulatory compliance, and localisation norms, impacting overall cost structures.' The segment commentary confirms that higher manpower, logistics and maintenance costs partly offset the superior Saudi yield advantage, with the Saudi business only beginning to generate positive monthly EBITDA - so the growth engine carries a margin-dilution risk while it scales.
risks.risk: Cost structure and localisation burden in new international geographies

risks.note: A structural concentration disclosed without being labelled a risk: BRSR Section A states crane hiring services account for 93.36% of turnover (Project EPC 6.63%), exports are 0% of turnover, and international markets served are stated as 0 countries. Notwithstanding the Saudi Arabia, Botswana and Qatar entities, the disclosed revenue base is overwhelmingly one activity in one country, so a domestic capex-cycle downturn or a single-sector demand shock transmits with little offset. (BRSR item 23 and the concentration items are read from the routed BRSR pages in this bundle.)

BRSR turnover rates jumped to 42.47% for permanent employees (18.22%/30.77%/19.06% split the prior year) and 77.00% for permanent workers (2.52% prior year) in FY2025-26 - the Company attributes this to Elevate 2030 growth and expansion. Separately, BRSR material issue 7 'Operational Health & Safety' flags accident, injury and fatality risk, 'especially among temporary workers who may lack sufficient training or experience', with serious incidents capable of causing project delays and downtime. For a business whose moat is stated to be execution and safety, a >40% attrition rate is a structural capability risk.
risks.risk: Workforce attrition and occupational health & safety exposure
